messages.content: How does AlphaFold 3 model protein structures differently from AlphaFold 2? Show the SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein (PDB 6VXX) in 3D with the receptor-binding domain highlighted, and cite the papers in my library.

AlphaFold 3 changes two things relative to AlphaFold 2. Its trunk does much less with the MSA, and its geometry-based structure module is replaced by a generative diffusion model that outputs raw atom coordinates. Together these let one network predict complexes of proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, ions and modified residues. Below, the details for AlphaFold 3 come from the summary of the AlphaFold 3 paper in your library. The library's AlphaFold 2 entry has no summary, so the AlphaFold 2 details are from my own knowledge of that paper.

## Representation: residues versus tokens

[AlphaFold 2](/paper/fc2d36b5-a8fe-4b20-a824-6b8815a45f7b) is built around amino acids. Each residue has a rigid backbone frame $T_i = (R_i, \vec t_i) \in SE(3)$, and side chains are rebuilt from up to seven torsion angles per residue type. That is very effective for proteins, but each new chemical entity would need its own hand-written parameterisation.

[AlphaFold 3](/paper/423df162-7d89-4df4-9022-e96643aaa393) uses a general tokenisation. Each standard residue or nucleotide is one token. Each heavy atom of a ligand or modified residue is its own token. Atom-level transformers encode atom features into token features before the trunk, and decode token features back to atoms inside the diffusion module. No frames or torsions are defined for any residue type. This is what lets one architecture handle arbitrary chemistry.

## Trunk: Evoformer versus Pairformer

The AlphaFold 2 Evoformer (48 blocks) keeps two representations in step:

- an MSA representation of size $N_\text{seq}\times N_\text{res}\times c_m$;
- a pair representation $z_{ij}$.

Information passes between them through row and column attention, an outer-product mean and triangle updates. Coevolution in the MSA is read out repeatedly throughout the network.

AlphaFold 3 cuts the MSA processing down to a small MSA module of 4 blocks that uses pair-weighted averaging. The main trunk is the **Pairformer** (48 blocks), which works only on a pair representation ($n\times n\times 128$) and a single representation ($n\times 384$). The MSA representation is not carried beyond the MSA module. Triangle multiplicative updates and triangle attention over $z_{ij}$ remain the core operations, and the single representation is updated by attention whose logits are biased by $z$. Recycling is kept.

Your library has mechanistic support for what this trunk does, from work on the open AlphaFold 3-style model Boltz-1. [How Do Co-folding Models Organize Structural Information?](/paper/88c0d7c6-c1ec-4b4e-a0a3-3107f9dc681e) finds that intra-chain distance information is already linearly decodable when the Pairformer starts (probe $R^2\approx 0.3$), so it comes mostly from MSA preconditioning. Inter-chain distance information, by contrast, is built up gradually across Pairformer layers and recycles. In other words, after the MSA module the Pairformer's main job is assembling the complex.

## Structure generation: invariant point attention versus diffusion

The AlphaFold 2 structure module has 8 blocks with shared weights. It uses **invariant point attention (IPA)** to update the per-residue frames, which makes it SE(3)-equivariant by construction. It is trained with the frame-aligned point error (FAPE) loss plus explicit losses for stereochemical violations (bond lengths and angles, clashes). It is deterministic: one input gives one structure.

AlphaFold 3 replaces this with a **diffusion module** (3 atom-level blocks, 24 token-level blocks, then 3 more atom-level blocks). Training noises the atom coordinates and teaches the network to predict the clean ones:

$$
\mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{x}_0 + \sigma_t\,\boldsymbol{\epsilon},\qquad
\mathcal{L} \propto \mathbb{E}_{\sigma_t,\boldsymbol\epsilon}\, w(\sigma_t)\,\big\|D_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t;\sigma_t, s, z) - \mathbf{x}_0\big\|^2 + \text{(smooth-LDDT, bond terms)}
$$

At inference, about 20 denoising steps start from Gaussian noise. Different noise levels carry different information: low noise teaches local stereochemistry and high noise teaches global arrangement. Because of this, AlphaFold 3 needs **no torsion parameterisation and no stereochemical violation losses**. It also does **not build in rotational equivariance**; random rotations and translations during training stand in for it.

The design has three consequences:

- **The model is generative.** Different seeds give different structures, and ranking many samples matters. For antibody–antigen complexes the paper's gains come from ranking across 1,000 seeds.
- **Hallucination is a risk.** Diffusion can invent ordered structure in disordered regions. AlphaFold 3 counters this by **cross-distillation**: it trains on AlphaFold-Multimer v2.3 predictions, where disorder appears as extended loops.
- **Confidence has to be trained differently.** Confidence heads (pLDDT, PAE and a new pairwise distance error, PDE) cannot be trained on a single forward pass. AlphaFold 3 runs a "mini-rollout" during training, generating full structures with large diffusion steps.

## Accuracy

The AlphaFold 3 paper reports these benchmark results:

| Benchmark | Result |
|---|---|
| PoseBusters v1 protein–ligand ($n=428$) | 76.0% within 2 Å pocket-aligned ligand RMSD, using only sequence and SMILES; far ahead of RoseTTAFold All-Atom ($P=4.45\times10^{-25}$) |
| Protein–protein ($n=1{,}064$ clusters) | Better than AlphaFold-Multimer v2.3 ($P=1.8\times10^{-18}$) |
| Protein–nucleic acid | Better than RoseTTAFold2NA on both protein–RNA and protein–dsDNA sets |
| Protein monomers | Better LDDT than AlphaFold 2 ($P=1.7\times10^{-34}$) |

## The diffusion boundary in practice

Splitting the model into a trunk and a diffusion module creates a boundary that can be measured. In Boltz-1, [Probing and steering biology across Boltz-1's trunk–diffusion boundary](/paper/f3c7e480-74ca-41ee-a913-7536162d9ce4) finds:

- Secondary structure crosses the boundary almost unchanged.
- Sequence chemistry is strongly attenuated. For example, the signal-peptide probe drops from F1 0.76 to 0.35.
- A β-strand direction that is highly decodable (F1 0.82) cannot be used to steer the predicted structure.

The co-folding analysis above also finds that ligand-induced backbone changes are not fully resolved in the trunk. The diffusion module has to reconcile intra- and inter-chain constraints that partly conflict, a role AlphaFold 2's structure module never had.

The same atom-level diffusion idea has been carried over to design. [RFdiffusion3](/paper/c7355659-26db-46f6-811a-9a04066d0d6a) uses AlphaFold 3-style all-atom diffusion with a cut-down 2-layer Pairformer to scaffold catalytic sites at atomic resolution.

## SARS-CoV-2 spike, closed prefusion state (PDB 6VXX)

```structure
{"title": "SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein, closed prefusion trimer (6VXX)",
 "models": [{"pdb": "6VXX", "color": "grey", "chainColors": {"A": "#9aa5b1", "B": "#c3cad3", "C": "#dfe3e8"}}],
 "highlights": [
   {"label": "RBD, chain A", "chain": "A", "resi": "319-541", "color": "warm"},
   {"label": "RBD, chain B", "chain": "B", "resi": "319-541", "color": "accent"},
   {"label": "RBD, chain C", "chain": "C", "resi": "319-541", "color": "violet"},
   {"label": "N-linked glycans (NAG)", "hetero": true, "resn": ["NAG"], "style": "sticks", "color": "green"}],
 "focus": "RBD, chain A",
 "caption": "In 6VXX all three receptor-binding domains (residues 319–541) are in the 'down' conformation, packed at the trimer apex, so the ACE2-binding ridge is occluded."}
```

6VXX is the cryo-EM structure of the trimer in its closed state, with all three RBDs down (Walls et al., *Cell* 2020; this paper is not in your library). The structure contains N-linked glycans, which AlphaFold 2 cannot represent but AlphaFold 3 handles as covalently attached ligand tokens. On the paper's glycan benchmark, AlphaFold 3 reaches 42.1% success for multi-residue glycans ($n=131$).

The spike also shows a shared weakness of both models: they predict one dominant state. The RBD switches between "down" and "up" conformations, and a deterministic AlphaFold 2 or a seed-sampled AlphaFold 3 usually returns only one of them. [Biasing Conformational Sampling in AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2 via Pair Representation Scaling](/paper/48d8e28d-5476-4830-bd13-0e3d1b19dd2a) and [ConforNets](/paper/9d4c76cb-a335-4157-9b5e-95f38585383c) both try to fix this by intervening on the trunk.

## Further reading

- [Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold](/paper/fc2d36b5-a8fe-4b20-a824-6b8815a45f7b) (Jumper et al., 2021), including its Supplementary Information on Evoformer, IPA and FAPE.
- [Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3](/paper/423df162-7d89-4df4-9022-e96643aaa393) (Abramson et al., 2024).
- [Protenix — Advancing Structure Prediction Through a Comprehensive AlphaFold 3 Reproduction](/paper/92445c82-aba0-40f2-9651-95d121355b0f), an open re-implementation that is useful for architectural details.
- [Benchmarking all-atom biomolecular structure prediction with FoldBench](/paper/ba6a0f33-651f-45f1-b734-8f5163de80ec), which independently evaluates AlphaFold 3-class models.
- [Structural Memorization in AlphaFold](/paper/6cf55a8a-4fea-485c-869f-107e83a4e778), on how much these models rely on templates.

spec.title: Evoformer (AlphaFold 2) vs Pairformer (AlphaFold 3)
spec.caption: The trunk change from Evoformer to a slimmer MSA module plus Pairformer is the core architectural difference in how AlphaFold 3 processes evolutionary and pairwise information before predicting structure.
spec.body_markdown:
**Evoformer (AF2).** The trunk of AlphaFold 2 has 48 blocks that jointly update an MSA representation and a pair representation. Information moves in both directions between them: MSA row and column attention is biased by the pair representation, and the MSA feeds back into the pair representation through an outer-product mean. Triangle multiplicative updates and triangle attention enforce geometric consistency on the pair representation [1].

**Pairformer (AF3).** AlphaFold 3 reduces the role of the MSA. A small MSA module of 4 blocks passes sequence-alignment information into the pair representation, using pair-weighted averaging. After that, the MSA is no longer carried forward [2]. A 48-block Pairformer then operates only on the pair representation (n×n×128) and the single representation (n×384). It uses triangle updates and attention, and the single representation attends with a bias from the pair representation [2].

**Connection to the question.** In AF2, the Evoformer output feeds a structure module that works on residue frames. AF3 replaces that module with a diffusion module that predicts atom coordinates directly. This lets it model general complexes, including proteins, nucleic acids, ligands and ions [2]. Both models share the triangle-update idea for pair features. The main difference is that AF3 drops the heavy MSA-centric processing.

spec.title: AlphaFold 3 diffusion training loss
spec.caption: AF3 trains a diffusion denoiser to recover clean atom coordinates from noised ones, using a noise-weighted MSE plus smooth-LDDT and bond-length terms, so the model learns structure directly at the atom level.

steps.explanation: Clean atom coordinates x_0 are corrupted with Gaussian noise at noise level sigma_t.
The denoiser, conditioned on the single representation s and pair representation z, predicts the clean coordinates directly.
The reconstruction error is a mean squared error weighted by w(sigma_t) to balance different noise levels.
Smooth-LDDT adds a local-distance accuracy term and the bond term penalizes bond-geometry errors, giving the full training loss.

423df162-7d89-4df4-9022-e96643aaa393.summary:
## Contribution
AlphaFold 3 (AF3) is a unified deep-learning model that predicts the joint 3D structure of biomolecular complexes containing proteins, nucleic acids (DNA/RNA), small-molecule ligands, ions, and covalently modified residues. Its core novelty over AlphaFold 2 (AF2) lies in (1) replacing the Evoformer with a simpler Pairformer that de-emphasizes MSA processing, and (2) replacing the structure module (which used amino-acid-specific frames and torsion angles) with a diffusion-based generative module that directly predicts raw atom coordinates, thereby naturally accommodating arbitrary chemical entities without stereochemical losses or special-case handling. AF3 achieves substantially higher accuracy than prior specialized tools across nearly all biomolecular interaction categories within a single model.

88c0d7c6-c1ec-4b4e-a0a3-3107f9dc681e.venue: 2026 Workshop on Generative and Agentic AI for Biology (ICML 2026)
88c0d7c6-c1ec-4b4e-a0a3-3107f9dc681e.summary:
## Contribution
This paper provides a mechanistic analysis of how co-folding models (specifically the Boltz-1 architecture) organize and evolve structural information within their internal representations. The authors move beyond single-chain analysis to investigate how multi-chain-specific representations—specifically the decomposition of the pair representation into intra-chain and inter-chain blocks—support joint biomolecular structure prediction. They identify three distinct information streams (single representation, intra-chain pair, and inter-chain pair) and characterize their functional roles, their evolutionary trajectory through the model depth (the "Mix–Compress–Refine" pattern), and the extent to which the diffusion module compensates for incomplete trunk representations.

## Methods
The researchers employ four distinct analytical "lenses" to study the Boltz-1 trunk:
1.  **Ablation (Interventional):** They apply zeroing, mean-only, and Gaussian (mean + variance) substitutions to the single representation ($S$), intra-chain pair ($Z_{intra}$), and inter-chain pair ($Z_{inter}$) blocks. This isolates whether the downstream diffusion module can still predict accurate structures when specific information streams are removed or randomized. …

f3c7e480-74ca-41ee-a913-7536162d9ce4.title: Probing and steering biology across Boltz-1’s trunk–diffusion boundary
f3c7e480-74ca-41ee-a913-7536162d9ce4.summary:
## Contribution
This paper investigates the representational shift of biological information as it moves from the representation-learning "trunk" to the coordinate-generating "diffusion" module in the Boltz-1 protein structure prediction model. The authors demonstrate that while the Pairformer trunk preserves both structural geometry and sequence chemistry, the diffusion module preserves geometry but significantly attenuates sequence chemistry. Furthermore, the study reveals that linear decodability of a feature does not guarantee causal steerability, specifically showing that highly predictive $\beta$-strand features in the trunk cannot be used to steer structure generation.

## Methods
The authors analyze per-residue activations from Boltz-1, extracting data from the 48-layer Pairformer trunk (every second layer) and the diffusion module (every second layer and every sampling step). They employ three primary analytical techniques:
1.  **Linear Probes:** Logistic regression probes trained on raw activations to measure decodability.
2.  **Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs):** TopK SAEs ($k=256$, 2048 latents) trained with $\ell_2$ regularization on demeaned activations to identify latent features. …

c7355659-26db-46f6-811a-9a04066d0d6a.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
c7355659-26db-46f6-811a-9a04066d0d6a.summary:
## Contribution
RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) is a generative artificial intelligence framework for the de novo design of biopolymers (proteins and nucleic acids) at an all-atom resolution. Unlike its predecessors (RFdiffusion1 and 2), which primarily operate at the amino acid residue level, RFD3 enables precise atomic-level control over functional sites, such as enzyme active sites and ligand-binding pockets. This allows for the design of complex interactions with non-protein components (small molecules, RNA, and DNA) within a unified, multi-modal generative framework.

## Methods
RFD3 employs an all-atom diffusion process utilizing a transformer-based U-Net architecture. The architecture consists of three primary components: (i) a downsampling module for encoding atomic and residue-level features, (ii) a sparse transformer module for token-wise information processing using distance-based attention to focus on local interactions, and (iii) an upsampling module that uses cross-attention to modulate atomic features with token-level features to predict coordinate updates. …

48d8e28d-5476-4830-bd13-0e3d1b19dd2a.title: Biasing Conformational Sampling in AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2 via Pair Representation Scaling
48d8e28d-5476-4830-bd13-0e3d1b19dd2a.summary:
## Contribution
The paper introduces **Boltz-sample**, a systematic steering strategy for the Boltz-2 protein structure prediction model that enables the recovery of alternative protein conformations. Unlike existing heuristic methods that rely on unpredictable input perturbations (such as Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) subsampling), Boltz-sample modulates the conformational landscape by uniformly rescaling the latent pair representation with a single scalar parameter $\beta$. This method provides a transparent and efficient way to navigate the model's latent space to improve ensemble coverage and dual-state recovery.

## Methods
The technical approach involves an inference-time intervention applied to the **Boltz-2** architecture, which consists of a Pairformer trunk and a diffusion-based structure generator. 
1.  **Latent Scaling:** The core mechanism is the uniform rescaling of the latent pair representation $z_{ij} \in \mathbb{R}^{dP}$ at the input to the Pairformer during each recycle step: $z^{scaled}_{ij} = (1 + \beta)z_{ij}$. 
2.  **Parameterization:** The scalar $\beta$ acts as a control handle for the effective strength of pairwise couplings. $\beta > 0$ strengthens coevolutionary and geometric constraints, while $\beta < 0$ relaxes them to facilitate the exploration of alternative states. …

9d4c76cb-a335-4157-9b5e-95f38585383c.title: ConforNets: Latents-Based Conformational Control in OpenFold3
9d4c76cb-a335-4157-9b5e-95f38585383c.summary:
## Contribution
ConforNets introduces a method for conformational control in AlphaFold3 (AF3)-based architectures by applying channel-wise affine transformations to the pair representations immediately preceding the Pairformer module. Unlike prior methods that perturb input MSAs or coordinate-space diffusion, ConforNets provides a global, reusable mechanism to modulate the conditioning signal. The core contribution is twofold: (1) an unsupervised method to discover multiple conformational states by maximizing pairwise distance in latent or coordinate space, and (2) a supervised "conformational transfer" method that learns to induce conserved structural changes across entire protein families using a single source protein.

## Methods
The technical approach utilizes the OpenFold3-preview (OF3p) architecture. The method intervenes at the latent level: specifically, the pair representation $z_{pre}$ before the Pairformer is transformed via an affine mapping $\phi(h) = hW^\top + b$, where $W$ and $b$ are trainable parameters initialized as identity and zero, respectively.

**1. Unsupervised Prediction:** To find alternate states, $k$ ConforNets are jointly optimized to maximize the distance between generated samples. The optimization uses gradient descent on two primary objectives: …

92445c82-aba0-40f2-9651-95d121355b0f.title: Protenix — Advancing Structure Prediction Through a Comprehensive AlphaFold 3 Reproduction
92445c82-aba0-40f2-9651-95d121355b0f.summary:
## Contribution
Protenix is an open-source reproduction of AlphaFold 3 (AF3) designed to democratize access to high-performance biomolecular structure prediction. The authors provide a complete implementation that refines ambiguous methodological steps and corrects typographical errors found in the original AF3 documentation. The primary contribution is a fully functional, trainable, and open-source model that achieves performance comparable to AF3 across protein-ligand, protein-protein, and protein-nucleic acid complexes, thereby facilitating downstream research and fine-tuning.

## Methods
The technical approach implements the architecture described in the AF3 framework. Protenix utilizes a single model trained on a consolidated dataset (unlike AF3's dual-model approach) to account for resource limitations. The model architecture includes a confidence head used for sample ranking; the authors specifically modified this head to improve performance. For protein-ligand tasks, the authors incorporate a penalty term in the score function during sample ranking to mitigate stereochemistry violations (e.g., incorrect chirality or steric clashes). …

ba6a0f33-651f-45f1-b734-8f5163de80ec.title: Benchmarking all-atom biomolecular structure prediction with FoldBench
ba6a0f33-651f-45f1-b734-8f5163de80ec.summary:
## Contribution
The authors introduce **FoldBench**, a unified, low-homology benchmark designed to systematically evaluate all-atom biomolecular structure prediction models across diverse interaction types. Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on single tasks or limited molecular classes, FoldBench provides a cross-domain assessment of proteins, nucleic acids, and ligands. The work identifies critical performance gaps, specifically demonstrating how model accuracy is highly dependent on training set similarity and highlighting the extreme difficulty of antibody-antigen and allosteric site prediction.

## Methods
The researchers curated a dataset of 1,522 biological assemblies from the Protein Data Bank (PDB), ensuring low homology to prevent data leakage and memorization. The benchmark covers nine prediction tasks: monomers (protein, RNA, DNA) and six interface types (protein-protein, antibody-antigen, protein-ligand, protein-RNA, protein-DNA, and protein-peptide). 

The study evaluates five state-of-the-art all-atom predictors: **AlphaFold 3, Boltz-1, Chai-1, HelixFold 3, and Protenix**. Prediction generation utilized a $5 \times 5$ sampling strategy (5 seeds $\times$ 5 samples) with 10 recycles per model to explore conformational space. Performance is quantified using:
*   **DockQ**: Success rate defined as the ratio of predictions with a DockQ score $\ge 0.23$. …

6cf55a8a-4fea-485c-869f-107e83a4e778.title: Structural Memorization in AlphaFold: Adversarial Mutations Reveal Template Reliance, Confidence Failures, and Implications for Protein Design
6cf55a8a-4fea-485c-869f-107e83a4e778.venue: ICML 2026 Workshop on Memorization in Foundation Models
6cf55a8a-4fea-485c-869f-107e83a4e778.summary:
## Contribution
This paper investigates whether AlphaFold 3 (AF3) learns generalizable biophysical principles or relies on structural memorization (template matching). Through adversarial mutation experiments, the authors demonstrate that AF3 exhibits extreme structural invariance to sequence perturbations—including destabilizing mutations and deletions—suggesting the model retrieves memorized templates rather than computing structures from first principles. The work highlights critical failures in AF3's confidence metrics and its inability to predict conformational changes in fold-switching proteins.

## Methods
The researchers employed an adversarial evaluation framework consisting of three primary regimes:
1.  **Point Mutations:** 200 protein sequences (categorized by monomer/multimer and similarity to training set) were subjected to maximally disruptive substitutions at 5%, 10%, 20%, 40%, and 70% residue thresholds.
2.  **Deletion Mutations:** Sequences were subjected to sparse residue deletions at 1%, 3%, 5%, and 10% thresholds, targeting central positions.
3.  **Comparative Analysis:** Results were benchmarked against ESMFold (a protein language model) to assess whether structural invariance is a general feature of deep learning or specific to AF3's architecture/training. …
